summary.headline: RHI Magnesita India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR1,014 crore and EBITDA rose 42% to INR147 crore, a 14.5% margin; management keeps the 13% FY27 margin guidance.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR1,014 crore, up 9% QoQ and 6% YoY, led by the steel business on favourable realizations and healthy demand. EBITDA grew 42% YoY to INR147 crore and margin expanded to 14.5% from 10.8%, which management attributed to steelmaking execution, price realisation and operating leverage. PAT nearly doubled to INR65 crore from INR35 crore. Management said price increases were largely war surcharges, and it kept FY27 guidance of 13% EBITDA margin and 7-8% volume growth, while stating 9% is a stretch. A leadership change was announced with Pankaj Malhan as MD and CEO, and Parmod Sagar continues as Chairman.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Main driver of Q1 revenue growth on favourable realisations and healthy demand; flow control business cited as the growth engine, with one large group's market share up almost twofold in about 6 months. Management said Dalmia business is flat and growth came from RHIM India.

segments.name: Cement
segments.commentary: Recovered in Q1 on seasonal maintenance demand; management said cement season is almost over by end-September.

segments.name: Industrial (non-ferrous, glass)
segments.commentary: Described as weak in Q1 with few projects in H1; silica and glass project orders expected in Q3-Q4.

segments.name: Coke oven project (PSU)
segments.commentary: Final-stage negotiation with pricing adjustment pending; production to start next month, with a 14-16 month project life.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 13% for FY27 reaffirmed; management said upside possible only if raw material costs ease.
Volume growth guidance of 7-8% for FY27 (management said 9% is a stretch); long-term volume guidance of steel/cement market growth plus 1-2%.
Management said the EUR45 million group pricing and mix benefit is already reflected in Q1 and that India will contribute proportionately.
Capex guidance of INR80-100 crore per year maintained, covering Dalmia plant modernisation, 4PRO machinery, robotics and maintenance.
MINPRO JV (51% RHIM, 49% Khemka) targeted to start production around Q4 FY27; initial investment about INR35 crore over two years, EBITDA 8-10%, payback under 3 years after production.
Quartzite mines (Chiraipani and Bhikampali) expected to open by end of Q1 FY27, with cost benefits from Q2.
Magnesite prices up 6-8% over the last two months; company is working on recipe optimisation and price pass-through.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR8 crore in Q1 vs INR150 crore guidance cited by an analyst; management kept the INR80-100 crore annual run-rate.
MINPRO greenfield mineral processing facility in Odisha, via JV with Khemka Refractories; roughly INR35 crore initial investment over two years.
Quartzite mines Chiraipani and Bhikampali came with the Dalmia deal; all licences received.
SAIL SMS4 expansion (about 6-6.5 million tonnes) expected to open refractory tenders in about 6-8 months.
Four or five products being transferred to India production within about one year (investor deck pages 21-22).
demand_pricing: Management cited steel production growth, high capacity utilisation and blast furnace/steelmaking investments as demand support; Indian steel grew 7-8% in H1 and steel capex of INR50,000-60,000 crore is expected this financial year.
Cement demand strong, but cement margins under pressure from fuel, energy and raw material costs.
Competitive pressure from domestic and multinational players, with greenfield and brownfield capacity additions and some excess capacity.
Exports reduced QoQ in Q1 per CFO; management expects isostatic flow control export growth over a year.
Alumina prices stable over the last six months; magnesite up 6-8% recently.
Realisation rise attributed mostly to war surcharges and product mix; no price/mix/FX split disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Split of ~12% realisation growth into price, mix and currency; sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: No split given. CFO said most price increases were war surcharges, so growth is primarily product-mix driven.

qa_highlights.question: Q1 capex only INR8 crore vs INR150 crore guidance; will guidance change?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term capex of INR80-100 crore a year unchanged; covers Dalmia modernisation, 4PRO robotics and maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Can volume growth of about 9% be achieved for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 7-8% is achievable but 9% is a stretch unless large high-volume orders come in.

qa_highlights.question: How should medium-term margins be viewed; split between Dalmia and RHIM India?
qa_highlights.answer: Dalmia flat; growth from RHIM India (flow control heavy, Bhiwadi and Jamshedpur). Medium-term margin supported by MINPRO and captive mines; no numeric range given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the EUR45 million group pricing benefit flow into India?
qa_highlights.answer: Benefit is group-wide across six regions; India contributes proportionately and it is already in Q1 numbers. FY27 margin guidance held at 13%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q1 numbers affected by project orders, and what is the H2 project pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: No project revenue in Q1. Coke oven project to start next month; glass and silica projects expected in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the quartzite mine and MINPRO JV deliver quantified savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Quantification still in progress by FP&A; management will share later. Mine opening expected by end-Q1 with benefits from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Auditor resignation and goodwill impairment?
qa_highlights.answer: Auditor change aligned with group auditor rotation; Dalmia goodwill fully written off, non-cash and below EBITDA, with headroom. No reversal planned.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (magnesite up 6-8%) and geopolitical risk (war surcharge dependence) could limit the 13% margin.
Volume guidance gap: H1 volume growth is below the 7-9% range, requiring a strong H2 for 7-8% growth.
Weak industrial segment until Q3-Q4 project orders (glass, silica) materialise.
Export volumes declined QoQ in Q1 and management has no near-term recovery timeline.
Capex run-rate far below the INR150 crore guidance cited by an analyst; check whether it catches up.
Execution on MINPRO (Q4 FY27 start) and quartzite mine (cost benefit from Q2).
CEO transition to Pankaj Malhan and auditor change at the AGM.
